title: JSON Formatter & Validator - Format, Minify & Sort Keys
description: Free online JSON formatter, validator, and minifier. Prettify with 2/4 spaces or tabs, sort keys, detect syntax errors with line numbers, and download.
quickAnswer: To format and validate JSON, paste your raw string into the editor. The tool parses the text via JSON.parse(), validates syntax, highlights exact error lines and column positions if invalid, and prettifies the structure with 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tabs. You can also minify to strip whitespace or sort keys alphabetically. Operates 100% in your browser.

commonMistakes.title: Trailing Commas
commonMistakes.description: Adding a comma after the final item in an array ([1, 2, 3,]) or object ({"a": 1,}) is valid in modern JavaScript but throws an immediate syntax error in standard JSON.

commonMistakes.title: Single Quotes for Strings
commonMistakes.description: JSON strictly requires double quotation marks ("key": "value"). Using single quotes ('key': 'value') is rejected by all compliant JSON parsers.

commonMistakes.title: Unquoted Object Keys
commonMistakes.description: In JavaScript, keys can omit quotes ({name: "value"}). In JSON, keys must always be enclosed in double quotes.

commonMistakes.title: Unescaped Control Characters
commonMistakes.description: Literal unescaped tab characters or raw unescaped newlines inside string values break JSON parsing and must be escaped as \t or \n.

faqs.q: What causes common JSON syntax errors?
faqs.a: The most frequent JSON syntax errors are trailing commas after the last array item or object property, unquoted keys, single quotes instead of double quotes, and unescaped newline characters inside strings.

faqs.q: Does this JSON formatter sort keys recursively?
faqs.a: Yes. When 'Sort keys alphabetically' is enabled, keys are sorted in alphabetical order at the top level and inside all nested child objects.

faqs.q: What is the maximum file size for formatting?
faqs.a: For browser safety and smooth responsiveness, the tool enforces a client-side safety limit of 1 MB (1,048,576 characters). Large payloads are debounced to prevent interface lag.

faqs.q: Is my JSON data uploaded to an external server?
faqs.a: No. All formatting, key sorting, validation, and minification happen 100% locally in your browser memory. Your confidential API keys, payload dumps, and configuration files are never sent over the network.

faqs.q: What is the difference between JSON formatting and minification?
faqs.a: Formatting adds indentation and line breaks so human developers can easily inspect and debug data. Minification strips all unnecessary whitespace to minimize payload bandwidth for network transmissions.

how-when-to-use-the-json.li1: Debugging REST & GraphQL APIs: Format unformatted single-line API responses from cURL or Postman into readable, nested structures.
how-when-to-use-the-json.li2: Validating Configuration Files: Quickly check tsconfig.json, package.json, or Kubernetes configurations for syntax mistakes before deploying.
how-when-to-use-the-json.li3: Payload Size Optimization: Minify JSON files prior to bundling or web transmission to reduce HTTP transfer size and bandwidth consumption.
how-when-to-use-the-json.li4: Deterministic Key Comparison: Use alphabetical key sorting to normalize two JSON documents so you can easily compare diffs without false key-order mismatches.

json-formatting-standards-indentation-fo.p1: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is a strict, text-based data interchange format specified in ECMA-404 and RFC 8259. Unlike JavaScript object literals, JSON requires double quotes around all keys and strings and strictly forbids trailing commas, comments, and unquoted identifiers.
